Q1: Stannous chloride exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). Additionally, it presents expanded perspective hazards (Tier 2) for endocrine disruption (EDC) and inhalation (IHL).
Q2: Stannous chloride is identified on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor. Concurrently, it appears on the EPA's "Substances Added to Food" list and FDA's GRAS list, suggesting low hazard under tightly regulated, very low quantity conditions, though it may still pose risks otherwise.
Q3: With 32,000 literature references, stannous chloride is extensively studied, placing it well above the median for chemicals in this dataset. It also has a significant number of toxicological records (119), indicating meaningful toxicological assessment, though it has not undergone the most rigorous EPA evaluations such as IRIS or PPRTV.
